attributes.description:
The estimator instance that defines the likelihood function
using the observed data.
attributes.name: base_estimator_

attributes.description:
The kernel used for prediction. In case of binary classification,
the structure of the kernel is the same as the one passed as parameter
but with optimized hyperparameters. In case of multi-class
classification, a CompoundKernel is returned which consists of the
different kernels used in the one-versus-rest classifiers.
attributes.name: kernel_

attributes.description: The number of classes in the training data
attributes.name: n_classes_

attributes.description:
Number of features seen during :term:`fit`.

.. versionadded:: 0.24
attributes.name: n_features_in_

attributes.description:
Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Defined only when `X`
has feature names that are all strings.

.. versionadded:: 1.0
attributes.name: feature_names_in_

methods.name: get_metadata_routing
methods.summary: Get metadata routing of this object.

parameters.description:
The kernel specifying the covariance function of the GP. If None is
passed, the kernel "1.0 * RBF(1.0)" is used as default. Note that
the kernel's hyperparameters are optimized during fitting. Also kernel
cannot be a `CompoundKernel`.
parameters.name: kernel

parameters.description:
Can either be one of the internally supported optimizers for optimizing
the kernel's parameters, specified by a string, or an externally
defined optimizer passed as a callable. If a callable is passed, it
must have the  signature::

    def optimizer(obj_func, initial_theta, bounds):
        # * 'obj_func' is the objective function to be maximized, which
        #   takes the hyperparameters theta as parameter and an
        #   optional flag eval_gradient, which determines if the
        #   gradient is returned additionally to the function value
        # * 'initial_theta': the initial value for theta, which can be
        #   used by local optimizers
        # * 'bounds': the bounds on the values of theta
        ....
        # Returned are the best found hyperparameters theta and
        # the corresponding value of the target function.
        return theta_opt, func_min

Per default, the 'L-BFGS-B' algorithm from scipy.optimize.minimize
is used. If None is passed, the kernel's parameters are kept fixed.
Available internal optimizers are::

    'fmin_l_bfgs_b'
parameters.name: optimizer

parameters.description:
The number of restarts of the optimizer for finding the kernel's
parameters which maximize the log-marginal likelihood. The first run
of the optimizer is performed from the kernel's initial parameters,
the remaining ones (if any) from thetas sampled log-uniform randomly
from the space of allowed theta-values. If greater than 0, all bounds
must be finite. Note that n_restarts_optimizer=0 implies that one
run is performed.
parameters.name: n_restarts_optimizer

parameters.description:
The maximum number of iterations in Newton's method for approximating
the posterior during predict. Smaller values will reduce computation
time at the cost of worse results.
parameters.name: max_iter_predict

parameters.description:
If warm-starts are enabled, the solution of the last Newton iteration
on the Laplace approximation of the posterior mode is used as
initialization for the next call of _posterior_mode(). This can speed
up convergence when _posterior_mode is called several times on similar
problems as in hyperparameter optimization. See :term:`the Glossary
<warm_start>`.
parameters.name: warm_start

parameters.description:
If True, a persistent copy of the training data is stored in the
object. Otherwise, just a reference to the training data is stored,
which might cause predictions to change if the data is modified
externally.
parameters.name: copy_X_train

parameters.description:
Determines random number generation used to initialize the centers.
Pass an int for reproducible results across multiple function calls.
See :term:`Glossary <random_state>`.
parameters.name: random_state
parameters.type_doc: int, RandomState instance or None, default=None

parameters.description:
Specifies how multi-class classification problems are handled.
Supported are 'one_vs_rest' and 'one_vs_one'. In 'one_vs_rest',
one binary Gaussian process classifier is fitted for each class, which
is trained to separate this class from the rest. In 'one_vs_one', one
binary Gaussian process classifier is fitted for each pair of classes,
which is trained to separate these two classes. The predictions of
these binary predictors are combined into multi-class predictions.
Note that 'one_vs_one' does not support predicting probability
estimates.
parameters.name: multi_class

parameters.description:
The number of jobs to use for the computation: the specified
multiclass problems are computed in parallel.
``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
``-1`` means using all processors. See :term:`Glossary <n_jobs>`
for more details.
parameters.name: n_jobs

signature: GaussianProcessClassifier(kernel=None, *, optimizer='fmin_l_bfgs_b', n_restarts_optimizer=0, max_iter_predict=100, warm_start=False, copy_X_train=True, random_state=None, multi_class='one_vs_rest', n_jobs=None)
summary: Gaussian process classification (GPC) based on Laplace approximation.
